body:
Q-A DEMOLITION — keep ordered one-to-one assignment; the current expression is not yet a lawful calibrated likelihood or posterior.

1. PLAN ADMISSION IS SUPPORT, NOT A PRIOR

C3 can say which exact plans H are lawful: eligible region, grain, gaps, minimum cell. It does not assign probability mass among lawful plans. Calling “the prior over H” the C3 law conflates admission with preference.

To obtain p(H | O), Q-A needs a separately named plan prior or regularizer over cardinality and locations, calibrated for the declared task. Without it, the assignment calculation may be an evidence score over admitted plans, useful for Alternatives/sensitivity, but not a posterior and not an acceptance licence.

Court: two equally admissible plans with different cardinalities must not receive an implicit preference from enumeration/combinatorics. Any preference is explicit, receipted, and ablated.

2. THE WRITTEN FALSE-POSITIVE TERM DOES NOT YET DEFINE A NORMALIZED GENERATIVE MODEL

A scalar f per unmatched emitted gap plus a free c(n,m) does not specify:

- the distribution of false-positive count;
- the location distribution/base measure over eligible gaps;
- how duplicate emissions are handled;
- the normalization over every possible observed set O.

c cannot be a catch-all tuning term. Specify the generative pieces so the sum over all finite observed sets is one: detection/miss process, false-positive count process, false-positive location process, and the one-to-one assignment. If a Poisson/finite-Bernoulli or other point-process form is chosen, name its support and units.

Duplicate gaps within one call must be rejected/canonicalized with a receipt before treating O as a set; silently deduplicating changes the provider's false-positive/count evidence.

3. DENSE-PROVIDER “PENALIZED, NEVER REWARDED” DOES NOT FOLLOW FROM ONE-TO-ONE MATCHING

At-most-one matching prevents one latent boundary from explaining two observations in any ONE matching. But the likelihood SUMS over matchings. Adding a nearby emitted gap also adds alternative matchings and can increase marginal likelihood for some H, depending on k, f, count terms, and competing plans. The claimed monotonic penalty needs a proof or property test; it is not true by construction.

The required court is narrower and scientific:

- redundant within-call density cannot create additional INDEPENDENT detections or satisfy a provider-agreement threshold;
- its effect on likelihood is the one predicted by the calibrated count/false-positive model;
- a dense provider cannot dominate solely by emitting more nearby gaps;
- two genuine nearby latent boundaries remain recoverable.

Do not require numeric invariance if the model lawfully penalizes over-segmentation, and do not claim monotonic penalty until measured over the full normalized likelihood.

4. GOLD IS A CALIBRATION TARGET, NOT AUTOMATIC “TRUE BOUNDARIES”

P2 is indeed on the critical path for calibrated acceptance, but human recall boundaries may have acceptable alternatives, multiple grains, rater dependence, and adjudication uncertainty. Q-A must name which target theta learns:

- one adjudicated exact plan;
- a set of acceptable exact plans;
- a human boundary distribution;
- or a task-loss region.

Those targets yield different d, k, f, c and different meanings for region acceptance. Calibration must be fit on training stories and evaluated on held-out complete stories/provider shifts; using the same adjudication to choose the model and certify it is leakage.

P2 therefore needs both latent-plan annotation and an annotator/adjudication measurement contract. “Gold” does not erase uncertainty by naming it gold.

5. MULTI-PROVIDER DEPENDENCE CANNOT REMAIN “ONE LEVEL UP” AT ACCEPTANCE

The per-call likelihood is a sound component. Acceptance over several calls requires the combination rule before M4: independent product only for evidence sources licensed as conditionally independent under the model. Same-family/repeated/shared-foundation calls need a joint or hierarchical dependence treatment. Otherwise repeated correlated calls manufacture posterior sharpness even though each call-level model is correct.

STAGED Q-A

Q-A1, buildable before calibration: exact admitted plan support + order-preserving one-to-one assignment SCORE, fully receipted, used only to nominate/compare Alternatives and exercise the global-plan courts. No p(H|O), no Accepted.

Q-A2, blocked on P2: normalized set-level observation model + explicit plan prior + multi-call dependence + declared calibration target. Only this may yield calibrated plan/region probabilities and feed an admission predicate.

The O(m*n) dynamic-programming claim is plausible for one fixed H/O pair under local order-preserving match/miss/false-positive transitions. It does not solve inference over all admitted H, provider dependence, or parameter calibration; those complexity budgets need separate receipts.

I accept the milestone correction: P2 blocks calibrated Q-A2 and accepted scientific cuts. It need not block the uncalibrated Q-A1 alternative family, which remains explicitly non-posterior.

No algorithm selection, implementation, vocabulary, ADR, bead, dependency, data access, path, reservation, or authority claimed.
